title: Prefill Shadowflow retro + action items
content:
Prefill Shadowflow — retro notes and concrete next steps

Context / TL;DR:
- This doc captures the 2029-09-30 cross-shift retro on the Shadowflow prefill experiment (kernel-level prefill + KV shadow caching + batch coalescing).
- Goal of the experiment: reduce p99 generation tail while keeping steady-state token/sec >= baseline and reduce cold-start evictions.
- Run window: 2029-09-24 -> 2029-09-29; traffic profile: 40% chat, 60% single-turn generation; median seq len 96.

Attendees:
- Lena Ortiz (owner)
- Marcus Chen (prefill + kernels)
- Priya Kapoor (telemetry + experiments)
- Omar Hafez (scheduler / batching)
- Zoe Martinez (SRE oncall)
- Notes pulled from: #infra-shadowflow, nightly run logs, and grafana snapshots.

What shipped in the run:
- Kernel patch: coalesce-prefill-v2 (PR 5123) — changes prefetch ordering and allows speculative attachment of KV pages to micro-batches.
- KV change: shadow-cache consistency toggle enabled for test cohort INF-2231. Eviction threshold relaxed from 0.6 -> 0.72 for shadow cohort.
- Batching change: reverter for long-tail splitting adjusted; batching window fixed at 6ms for speculative-prefill paths.

High-level outcomes (numbers from 2029-09-29 summary):
- p50 latency: baseline 38ms -> experiment 36ms (small improvement).
- p95: baseline 120ms -> experiment 108ms (-10%).
- p99: baseline 273ms -> experiment 197ms (-28%): major win for tail.
- tokens/sec (steady-state): baseline 78k -> experiment 74k (-5%); note this drop concentrated in heavy long-seq slices.
- KV evictions per host/hour: baseline 8.9 -> experiment 2.6 (-71%).
- GPU mem overhead: +3.1% on average (due to pinned prefill KV pages).
- Cost estimate (proxy): +2.6% compute cost per token for the cohort due to overheads; net UX improvement is positive for 3/4 of monitored customers.

Observed side-effects / anomalies:
- Regression on some long-seq tail flows where batching window prevented proper merging; manifested as brief token/sec dips for seq>512. See INF-2305 for repro steps.
- Two incidents where shadow-cache diverged during infra restart (SRE ticket created). Root cause appears to be ordering between KV attach and kernel rollback under transient OOM.
- A few customers (3) with high concurrency saw token/sec drop >12% for the cohort because their request mix forced many speculative prefill allocations that later rolled back.

What went well:
- Tail latency reduction at p99 is significant and stable across multiple regions (us-west, eu-west).
- Eviction reduction means warmer cache hit ratios for downstream canary traffic; fewer cold fills.
- Instrumentation added (per-request prefill tag) made triage much faster — big win for observability.

What didn't go well / lessons learned:
- Default eviction relaxation was too aggressive for multi-tenant hosts — need a per-tenant cap.
- Kernel rollback path under OOM wasn't thoroughly exercised; we need synthetic failure injectors for this code path.
- Our batching heuristics need to consider speculative prefill inflation; current window logic can hurt long-seq mixes.
- Experiment gating lacks per-customer ROI evaluation in the rollout pipeline.

Action items (owners + due dates):
1) Canary rollout plan for coalesce-prefill-v2 (Lena) — due 2029-10-07
   - Add per-tenant soft cap on prefetched KV pages (default 48MB).
   - Disable eviction threshold relaxation for enterprise-tagged hosts.
2) OOM rollback tests (Marcus) — due 2029-10-04
   - Add a fuzz harness that simulates transient OOM between KV-attach and kernel acceptance.
   - Push unit tests covering rollback ordering (PR template to reference INF-2305).
3) Batching heuristic tweak (Omar) — due 2029-10-10
   - Implement sequence-length aware batching window: increase window to 12ms for seq>256, keep 6ms for seq<=256.
   - Add a telemetry knob to flip window in runtime for fast rollback.
4) Telemetry dashboards and alerting (Priya) — due 2029-10-06
   - Add p99-per-seq-length panel and a prefetched-pages-per-request histogram.
   - Create an alert that fires when tokens/sec drops >10% for a hosted-customer over 10m with prefills enabled.
5) Postmortem & SRE follow-up (Zoe) — due 2029-10-05
   - Formalize runbook steps for shadow-cache divergence and link to oncall checklist.
   - Coordinate with infra to add graceful fallback when KV attach fails mid-flight.
6) Customer ROI review (Lena + Solutions Eng) — due 2029-10-14
   - Export sample traces for 10 affected customers and compute UX delta vs cost delta.

Open questions / discussion points:
- Should we make prefill per-route (route-level opt-in) instead of per-tenant? Pros: finer control for high-concurrency routes. Cons: rollout complexity.
- What threshold should gating use for rolling back in production? Current: absolute tokens/sec delta; maybe better to use p99 delta + customer-level ROI.
- Do we need a dedicated small-VM canary pool that enforces stricter eviction to validate memory foot prints?

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Try hybrid prefill: only prefill top-2 KV pages for speculative -> attach more if batch actually materializes. Could be low-risk win.
- Add a short-lived metric that tags prefills that are rolled back within 50ms — helps quantify wasted work.
- Consider combining with short-circuit-routing: if a request is long-seq and queue high, route to cached-optimized kernel variant.

Appendix: quick reproduction steps for INF-2305 (already added to ticket):
- Run the long-seq synthetic with concurrency=120, seq=640, batching-window=6ms, prefill-enabled. Observe token/sec dip ~30s after start. Collect core dump and kernel logs.
- Docker image: redwood/serving-runtime:prefill-exp-2029-09-21

Meeting adjourned. Next sync: 2029-10-07 (canary readiness check).

-- Lena
